name: multi-statement handler bodies and atomic handler replacement
status: LOCKED and built (patch_multi.py + replacement cascade_plan.py / cascade_vocab.json / harness_protocol.json); verified on Godot 4.3 with the stand-in mule, not yet on real Gemma
motivating_intent: when the player enters the scene, also print 'ready' (tree_entered already has a handler, and a handler's body cannot be edited today)

1_statement_schema.body: an array of 1 to 6 statement objects (the legacy string body with top-level property/type/operator/value/message still works and is read as a list of one)
1_statement_schema.type: optional on a statement; the harness fills it from the registry and GI_1 checks it
1_statement_schema.array_body_rules: message must be "" and property/type/operator/value must be absent at the top level; every statement obeys the rules it already has (registered property, operand type, no no-op operand, plain print charset)
list_rules: a property may be assigned (=) only once (a second = would erase the first) - NEW
the simulated net effect on every touched property must differ from its starting value, so += 50 then -= 50 is refused - NEW
at most 6 statements (each costs a mule call)
1_statement_schema.normalization: every consumer (canonical text, GI_1, GI_3, expectation, probe) works on statements_of(block), so single-statement blocks take the same code path with a list of one

2_atomic_replacement.slot: mode: add (default) or replace - NEW, an optional slot
2_atomic_replacement.add: the function must not exist, as today; an identical function is NOOP_ALREADY_DEFINED
2_atomic_replacement.replace: the function must exist; the whole function is swapped as one span; nothing else in the file moves
replace_rules_NEW: explicit: a plain add_method that hits an existing name is still refused (a mistyped name must never overwrite hand-written code); the refusal now says 'use mode replace'
only handlers: the name starts with _on_ and the function takes no arguments; engine callbacks (_physics_process, _ready ...) and functions with arguments are refused
the existing signature line must equal the canonical one (func name() -> void:), no annotation line sits directly above, so only the body changes
an identical function is a NOOP
2_atomic_replacement.mechanics: function_span(raw, fn) finds the 'func' line and its indented body, trailing blank lines stay in the gap; replace_function(raw, fn, text) swaps exactly that span; written as temp file + os.replace after a .bak backup; the existing reload check (found, arg_count 0, has_method) and rollback apply; the apply record keeps mode and the old body
2_atomic_replacement.connections: untouched: the signature is unchanged, so existing signal connections keep working
2_atomic_replacement.undo: the plan undo already restores the backup byte for byte

3_mule_containment.one_call_per_statement: the mule is asked for ONE line at a time. The prefill is the JSON head + the signature + the lines accepted so far + a newline; the mule completes one line and the answer is cut at the first quote
3_mule_containment.prefill_example:
..."stmt":"func _on_player_tree_entered() -> void:
    speed = 450.0
    velocity *= 2.0
   <- the mule writes only the third line
3_mule_containment.message: the ultra message shows only that statement's fields, in exactly the shape used today for assign / relative / print / pass, so the prompts and heat maps proven so far carry over
3_mule_containment.canonical_scaffold: the harness keeps its own canonical text for each accepted line (the script's indent, = / += spelling, double quotes), never the mule's spelling, so every later prefill is clean
3_mule_containment.gi3_per_line: the existing exact check on that one line; retries (3 tries, the same temperatures) are per statement; a line that fails 3 tries sends the whole frame to the dead letter, recording the statement number and the accepted prefix; nothing is written
3_mule_containment.one_judge_one_apply: after the last line the assembled function goes through ONE parse check (for replace: the whole script with the span swapped in a temporary copy) and ONE apply
never: a signature written by the mule
more than one statement spec in a prompt
more than one new line accepted per call (a longer answer fails the line count and retries)
3_mule_containment.unchanged_path: a single-statement add block keeps today's code path untouched
3_mule_containment.cost: about 4 to 5 seconds warm per statement (your real runs: 4.5 / 6.3 / 4.3 / 4.5 s); 3 statements about 13 s, 6 about 27 s; the model stays loaded across statements and blocks

4_probe.expectation: a list of statements: from the block, or read back line by line from the script for hand-written handlers (one unparseable line makes it UNVERIFIED)
4_probe.starting_values: set before the stimulus for EVERY touched property: the known baseline (100.0 / 100 / [10,20] / [10,20,30]) when its first statement is relative, a perturbed value (different from the first literal) when its first statement is an assignment
4_probe.isolation: on when any statement is relative: the node's other _on_ handlers are disconnected and its own processing is off, as in Step 12
4_probe.expected: simulate the whole list n times from the starting values (n = the measured emissions, 1 for a call or an explicit emit): a final value per property and the multiset of printed messages x n
assertions: every touched property: normal final equals the simulated final
every touched property: the control stays at its starting value
no other registered property differs between normal and control (the differential effect is exactly the touched set)
the printed lines of normal minus control equal the expected multiset (messages x n)
4_probe.report: one line listing every property (speed 100.0 -> 250.0, velocity [10, 20] -> [40, 95]) and the prints
4_probe.replace_extra_NEW: after a replace, the handler is also verified through each connection it already has in the scene, so a swapped body that no longer fires on its signal fails and rolls back
4_probe.feasibility_tested: a 5-statement list (assign, +=, print, *= and += on a Vector2) simulated from speed 100.0 / velocity (10, 20) over 2 runs gave speed 250.0, velocity (40, 95), two 'boosted' prints, and Godot gave exactly the same; the probe's perturbation argument accepts an array and still accepts the old single object

5_plan_tool.then: a single form as today, or a list of 1 to 6 of the existing forms: [{"set": ...}, {"increase": ...}, {"print": "x"}]
5_plan_tool.when: stays add-only; if the handler exists with a different body the refusal says to use change_handler
5_plan_tool.dry_run: a replace shows 'replaces: <old effect>' (hand-written bodies are flagged 'HAND-WRITTEN, N lines, WILL BE DISCARDED') so the user sees what disappears before saying go
5_plan_tool.catalog: handlers list every statement of their body and are marked [replaceable] (an _on_ handler with no arguments) or [not replaceable: engine callback / has arguments]
5_plan_tool.protocol: before a change_handler the goal sentence names what is replaced and what it does now, and waits for a yes; the repeat note applies to every relative statement

6_patch_design.files: patch_multi.py (clock and spec, per file with the patch library) + replacement cascade_plan.py, cascade_vocab.json, harness_protocol.json, patch_status.py
clock_regions: new section: statements_of, function_span, replace_function, simulate, expected_prints
body_line / canonical_function: the whole function from the list
add_method_checks: the array schema, the list rules, mode, replace rules
add_method_stmt_error: one line against the statement k, with the k lines before it already fixed
slot 3 in main(): a body-frame path (one call per statement) beside the untouched single-statement loop; the post-ACK part (judge, apply, verify, registry) becomes one function both paths call
handler_expectation: a list; reading back several lines
run_probe / PROBE_GD: an array of starting values; the multi-property verdict; replace re-verified through the scene's connections
op_fields, the ultra and slim views, _norm
tests_before_delivery: function_span / replace_function: middle of file, last function without a trailing newline, tabs, a comment above the next function, annotation above (refused)
the GI_1 matrix: the cap, pass alone, a doubled =, a net-zero list, replace of a missing function, an engine callback, a handler with arguments, a differing signature
the per-statement flow with the stand-in mule: 3 statements, one statement failing 3 tries (dead letter keeps the prefix), a retry that succeeds, a mule answering two lines at once (refused)
the probe: several properties plus prints, a neighbor that writes the same property, a hand-written multi-line handler read back, a replace verified through its connection, a rollback
the plan tool: change_handler dry run showing the replaced body, run, undo byte for byte, NOOP on an identical body

decisions_to_lock: 1. the statement schema, normalization and list rules (cap 6, pass alone, one = per property, net effect must differ)
2. mode add / replace with the replace rules: explicit, _on_ handlers with no arguments only, signature unchanged, old body shown and kept in the backup
3. one mule call per statement with the scaffolded prefill; the single-statement path untouched
4. the probe: simulation over all touched properties, starting values, isolation when relative, prints multiset, replace re-verified through existing connections
5. the plan tool: list then, change_handler, the replaced body in the dry run, catalog markers
6. delivery: patch_multi.py plus the replacement files
built_notes: type is REQUIRED inside assign / relative statements at block level (the plan tool fills it from the registry), because the canonical text is built without a host lookup
a 'then' list of one item keeps the single-statement path; two or more items, or a replacement, use the body-frame path
mode replace needs an array body; a legacy string body with mode replace is refused
the probe isolates the handler (neighbors disconnected, processing off) for every body frame, not only relative ones
heat-map recording keeps the picks of the last accepted statement of a body frame
